question.text: Aravalli Growth Fund (Category II, close-ended) plans to list its units on BSE for liquidity. Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which of the following conditions applies?

answer.text: Listing is mandatory for all close-ended AIFs within 90 days of first close
Listing is permitted immediately after in-principle approval from SEBI
Listing is VOLUNTARY; minimum tradable lot INR 1 crore; listing permitted only AFTER final close; Angel Fund units cannot be listed
Minimum tradable lot is INR 10 crore; only Cat I may list

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Listing of close-ended AIF units is VOLUNTARY (not mandatory). Conditions: (i) minimum tradable lot of INR 1 CRORE; (ii) listing permitted only AFTER FINAL CLOSE of the fund/scheme; (iii) application to the recognised stock exchange + SEBI approval; (iv) stock exchange grants final approval post SEBI nod. Units of ANGEL FUNDS shall NOT be listed. CDMDF units also cannot be listed. **The Trap:** Option A mandates listing (false). Option B jumps to in-principle phase (too early). Option D fabricates lot size and Cat restriction. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests listing mechanics. Compares with REIT/InvIT listing (mandatory, continuous trading). AIF listed units trade infrequently — the INR 1 crore lot deters retail volume. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Listing is most useful for debt-fund structures where secondary transfers can occur. Warn LPs that listing does NOT convert a close-ended fund to open-ended — no redemption, only secondary-market exit subject to available buyer. Build a market-making arrangement with a broker to provide two-way quotes.
